observations: Photo 0 and Photo 1 show a Yamaha keyboard with a blue control panel and white/black keys, partially wrapped in plastic.
The control panel has a digital display, buttons, and a grid of colored buttons (green, orange, red).
The keyboard appears to be in a retail or store environment, with other products visible in the background.
The plastic wrapping is still on the right side of the keyboard, suggesting it is new or recently unpacked.
No power cord, stand, or accessories are visible in the photos.
The seller claims 'Very good sound and quality Yamaha keyboard'.

claims.claim: Very good sound and quality Yamaha keyboard
claims.evidence: The photos show the physical appearance and packaging, but no sound test or internal condition is visible. The claim of 'very good sound' cannot be verified remotely.

risks.risk: The keyboard may not be functional or may have internal damage not visible in photos.
risks.proof: A video clip showing the keyboard powered on, keys responding, and sound output.

risks.risk: The keyboard may be missing accessories (power cord, stand, or manuals).
risks.proof: A photo showing all included accessories laid out next to the keyboard.

risks.risk: The keyboard may be a counterfeit or non-genuine Yamaha product.
risks.proof: A close-up of the serial number and model label, and a video of the keyboard being tested with a known sound source.

proof_requests: Video of the keyboard powered on and playing a note to verify sound quality.
Photo showing all included accessories (power cord, stand, manuals, etc.).
Close-up of the serial number and model label on the keyboard.
Photo of the keyboard without plastic wrapping to check for damage or wear.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
